title: NJ Driver's Manual – Chapter 2
subtitle: Before You Drive
note: Based on the 2025 NJ Driver's Manual, Chapter 2. Verify all answers against the current manual before your exam.

questions.q: Under New Jersey law, who is required to wear a seat belt in a passenger vehicle?
opts: Only the driver
Driver and front-seat passengers only
All occupants of the vehicle
Only adults 18 and older
questions.exp: NJ law requires every occupant of a passenger vehicle — front and back seats — to be buckled up.

questions.q: How should the shoulder portion of a seat belt be properly positioned?
opts: Behind your back for extra comfort
Under your arm to reduce chest pressure
Across your chest and over your shoulder, away from the neck
Across the abdomen
questions.exp: The shoulder belt should cross the chest diagonally. Routing it behind your back or under your arm severely reduces its effectiveness.

questions.q: Until what minimum age must a child ride in a rear-facing car seat in New Jersey?
opts: 6 months
1 year
2 years
4 years
questions.exp: NJ law requires children to remain rear-facing until at least 2 years old, or until they exceed the seat's height/weight limit.

questions.q: In NJ, children under age 8 who are also shorter than 57 inches must be secured in:
opts: An adult seat belt only
A rear-facing infant seat only
An appropriate child safety seat or booster seat
A forward-facing seat only
questions.exp: Children under 8 AND under 57 inches tall require a child restraint system (rear-facing, forward-facing, or booster, as appropriate for size).

questions.q: A child should NOT ride in the front passenger seat when:
opts: The driver is a new licensee
The vehicle is traveling above 40 mph
The front airbag is active and the child is in a rear-facing seat
The child is over 40 lbs
questions.exp: A rear-facing seat in front of an active airbag is extremely dangerous. Airbag deployment can fatally injure an infant. Children should always be in the back seat.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a head restraint?
opts: To keep the driver alert on long trips
To reduce whiplash injuries in rear-end collisions
To improve the driver's visibility to the rear
To support the neck during extended highway driving
questions.exp: Head restraints (headrests) are safety devices designed to limit rearward head movement and reduce whiplash injuries in rear-end crashes.

questions.q: For maximum protection, the top of the head restraint should be positioned:
opts: At chin level
At ear level
At or above the top of your head
As far back as possible
questions.exp: The top of the head restraint should be level with or above the top of your head to properly limit rearward head motion.

questions.q: For safety with a steering-wheel-mounted airbag, you should hold the wheel at:
opts: 10 and 2 o'clock
12 and 6 o'clock
9 and 3 o'clock (or 8 and 4)
One hand at 12 o'clock
questions.exp: Current safety guidance recommends 9 and 3 (or 8 and 4) to keep hands below the airbag deployment zone, reducing wrist and arm injury risk.

questions.q: Before starting your vehicle, you should first:
opts: Tune the radio to a traffic station
Check your mirrors, adjust your seat, and fasten your seat belt
Rev the engine briefly to warm it up
Turn on the hazard lights
questions.exp: Adjust your seat so controls are comfortably reachable, position all mirrors, and buckle your seat belt before starting the engine.

questions.q: How should the rearview mirror be adjusted?
opts: So you can see the rear bumper of your own vehicle
So the entire rear window is centered in the mirror
Angled to reduce headlight glare from vehicles behind
Pointed slightly downward for night driving
questions.exp: Center the rear window in the rearview mirror so you have the widest possible view of the road behind you.

questions.q: Side mirrors should be adjusted so that you can see:
opts: Mostly the side of your own vehicle
A small sliver of your own vehicle and the lane beside you
Only vehicles directly behind your rear bumper
The road immediately below your rear tires
questions.exp: A small strip of your own car at the inner edge of each side mirror confirms proper alignment; the rest shows the adjacent lane to minimize blind spots.

questions.q: You should NOT use cruise control when:
opts: Traveling on a straight interstate highway
Speed is steady and traffic is very light
In heavy traffic, rain, snow, or when you feel drowsy
Your vehicle is less than 5 years old
questions.exp: Cruise control is for open, steady-speed driving only. Wet or icy roads, heavy traffic, and fatigue all require your full manual control.

questions.q: A pregnant driver should wear a seat belt with the lap portion:
opts: Across the abdomen for fetal protection
As high on the stomach as possible
Snugly across the hips and upper thighs, below the abdomen
Omitted, to avoid abdominal pressure
questions.exp: The lap belt should fit low across the hip bones and upper thighs — never across the abdomen. The shoulder belt goes between the breasts and over the shoulder.

questions.q: What is the main danger of running a vehicle engine inside a closed garage?
opts: Battery drain
Carbon monoxide poisoning
Engine overheating
Fuel evaporation
questions.exp: Vehicle exhaust contains carbon monoxide (CO), an odorless, colorless gas that is rapidly fatal in enclosed spaces.

questions.q: NJ's child passenger safety law applies to children traveling in:
opts: Only the child's family-owned vehicle
Only vehicles with a rear seat
All passenger automobiles, vans, SUVs, and light trucks
Only school buses and day-care vans
questions.exp: The law covers all passenger vehicles — it does not matter who owns the vehicle or who is driving.

questions.q: What does the LATCH system provide for child safety seats?
opts: A temperature alarm if a child is left in a hot car
Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children — a built-in attachment system that secures seats without using seat belts
A federal registry for recalled car seats
An electronic lock that prevents the seat from sliding
questions.exp: LATCH (Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children) allows child safety seats to be installed securely using dedicated vehicle anchor points instead of — or in addition to — seat belts.

questions.q: When loading cargo into a vehicle, the heaviest items should be placed:
opts: On a roof rack for highest center of gravity
Behind the rear axle to improve traction
Low in the cargo area, centered and close to the floor
In the rear passenger footwells
questions.exp: Heavy cargo should ride low and centered. High or rear-heavy loads raise the center of gravity and can affect handling and braking.

questions.q: The primary risk of driving with an unsecured load is:
opts: Reduced fuel economy
Voiding the vehicle warranty
Cargo shifting or falling, creating road hazards for other drivers
Excessive tire wear
questions.exp: Unsecured loads can slide, tip, or fall from the vehicle, striking other motorists, pedestrians, or cyclists — causing serious injuries and potential criminal liability.

questions.q: If you feel drowsy behind the wheel, the safest action is to:
opts: Open the windows for fresh air and continue
Turn the music up loud
Drink a caffeinated beverage and drive on
Pull over in a safe location and sleep or rest
questions.exp: No short-term stimulant reliably overcomes drowsiness. Only rest restores alertness. Drowsy driving is a leading cause of serious crashes.

questions.q: In New Jersey, the legal blood alcohol content (BAC) limit for drivers 21 and older is:
questions.exp: A BAC of 0.08% or higher constitutes driving while intoxicated (DWI) in NJ for drivers 21 and older. For drivers under 21 the limit is 0.01%.

questions.q: Which statement about prescription medications and driving is correct?
opts: All prescription drugs are safe because a doctor authorized them
Only over-the-counter drugs impair driving
You should check with your doctor or pharmacist about any driving-related side effects before driving
Pain relievers sharpen reaction time and are always safe to drive on
questions.exp: Many prescription drugs — including pain relievers, antihistamines, and sedatives — can impair driving. Always consult your prescriber or pharmacist.

questions.q: Allowing a pet to ride loose inside the vehicle is dangerous because:
opts: It is illegal in all 50 states
It can distract the driver and become a projectile in a crash
Only large dogs are a distraction; small pets are safe
It lowers the vehicle's fuel efficiency significantly
questions.exp: An unrestrained pet can distract you while driving and, in a sudden stop or crash, become a dangerous high-speed projectile inside the cabin.

questions.q: If your accelerator pedal becomes stuck while driving, you should:
opts: Immediately yank up on the parking/emergency brake
Shift to reverse to slow the wheels
Keep both hands on the wheel, shift to neutral, slow down, and pull safely off the road
Turn the ignition off while the vehicle is moving
questions.exp: Shifting to neutral disconnects engine power without disabling steering. Brake gently to a stop. Turning off the ignition removes power steering and may lock the steering column.

questions.q: If a tire blows out while driving, the first correct action is to:
opts: Immediately brake hard to stop quickly
Grip the steering wheel firmly and gradually ease off the accelerator
Swerve immediately onto the shoulder
Shift to a lower gear first
questions.exp: Grip the wheel firmly to maintain directional control and allow the vehicle to slow naturally. Hard braking can cause a spin. Ease off the gas, then steer smoothly to the shoulder.

questions.q: A medical condition that may affect your license is one that:
opts: Requires you to take any daily medication
Is seasonal, such as allergies
Could cause a sudden loss of consciousness or significantly impair your ability to operate a vehicle
Makes you legally blind in only one eye
questions.exp: Conditions such as uncontrolled epilepsy or certain heart arrhythmias must be reported and may result in license suspension until medical clearance is obtained.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT typically part of a pre-trip vehicle inspection?
opts: Checking tire tread and inflation
Verifying all lights and signals work
Testing the radio and navigation system
Inspecting windshield wipers and washer fluid
questions.exp: A safety inspection covers mechanical and safety systems. The entertainment/navigation system is not a safety-critical item.

questions.q: The lap belt portion of a seat belt should fit:
opts: Across the soft tissue of the abdomen
As high on the waist as possible
Snugly across the hip bones and upper thighs
Loosely, so you can slide forward in your seat
questions.exp: Lap belts resting on soft abdominal tissue can cause serious internal injuries in a crash. Position the belt low across the hard bone of the hips.

questions.q: What does an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) do during hard braking?
opts: Stops the vehicle faster on all surfaces
Prevents the wheels from locking so you can steer during emergency braking
Automatically steers the vehicle away from hazards
Reduces fuel consumption during braking
questions.exp: ABS rapidly pulses the brakes to prevent wheel lockup, allowing you to maintain steering control while braking hard — which can help you avoid a collision.

questions.q: When backing out of a driveway, you should:
opts: Check the rearview mirror only
Sound the horn twice, then reverse quickly
Turn to look over your shoulder and check all mirrors; back slowly and smoothly
Rely entirely on the backup camera if equipped
questions.exp: Back cameras and mirrors have blind zones. Physically turning to look behind you, combined with mirror checks, gives the best view and minimizes risk to pedestrians, especially small children.

questions.q: A forward-facing child seat should be installed:
opts: In the front seat with the passenger airbag disabled
In the back seat, secured tightly with LATCH or seat belt, with the top tether attached to the anchor
In the back seat facing sideways for easy access
On the passenger-side front seat only when the airbag is turned off
questions.exp: Forward-facing seats belong in the back seat, secured as tightly as possible. The top tether significantly reduces forward head movement in a crash.

questions.q: NJ recommends (though does not legally mandate by age alone) that children ride in the back seat until at least:
opts: 4 years old
8 years old
12–13 years old
16 years old
questions.exp: All major safety organizations and the NJ MVC recommend that children under 13 ride in the back seat because front airbags are designed for adult bodies and can injure smaller children.

questions.q: The primary purpose of wearing a seat belt is to:
opts: Comply with the law and avoid a fine
Keep you in proper driving posture
Prevent you from being thrown from the vehicle or striking the interior during a crash
Ensure the airbag system activates correctly
questions.exp: Seat belts restrain occupants in their seats during a crash, preventing ejection from the vehicle and reducing impact forces on the body.

questions.q: If a vehicle's headlights fail, the driver should:
opts: Drive only at low speeds with hazard lights on
Use daytime running lights as a substitute
Not drive until the headlights are repaired
Drive only in well-lit urban areas
questions.exp: Driving without working headlights is both illegal and extremely dangerous. The vehicle must not be driven until repaired.

questions.q: Tire pressure should ideally be checked:
opts: Only when a tire visibly looks flat
Once a year at annual inspection
Monthly and before any long trip, when tires are cold
After every 10,000 miles of driving
questions.exp: Check tire pressure at least monthly and before long trips. Always check when tires are cold (not driven for 3+ hours) for the most accurate reading.

questions.q: "Cold tire pressure" means the pressure measured when:
opts: The outside air temperature is below freezing
Tires have not been driven on for at least 3 hours (or less than 1 mile from their storage location)
Using a digital rather than analog gauge
Tires were inflated in a cold-storage facility
questions.exp: Driving heats up tires and increases their internal pressure. The manufacturer's recommended pressure is for cold tires — tires that haven't been driven on recently.

questions.q: What does a booster seat do that makes it safer than a seat belt alone for a young child?
opts: Cushions the child against side impacts
Positions the child so the vehicle's seat belt fits properly across the chest and hips rather than the abdomen and neck
Prevents the front airbag from deploying
Anchors the child directly to the vehicle frame
questions.exp: Children have shorter torsos than adults. A booster seat elevates them so the shoulder belt crosses the chest (not the neck) and the lap belt rests on the hip bones (not the abdomen).

questions.q: An airbag is described as a "supplemental" restraint system because:
opts: It only supplements the driver, not passengers
It supplements the seat belt — it is NOT a replacement and offers little protection without a seat belt
It is standard only on newer vehicles
It supplements the ABS system
questions.exp: Airbags (SRS — Supplemental Restraint System) work in conjunction with seat belts. Unbelted occupants can be seriously injured by airbag deployment itself.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about carbon monoxide (CO) is TRUE?
opts: CO has a distinct rotten-egg smell that warns you to evacuate
CO is heavier than air and pools at floor level only
CO is colorless and odorless, making it undetectable without a detector
CO is only dangerous outdoors in high concentrations
questions.exp: Carbon monoxide is colorless, odorless, and tasteless — you cannot detect it by smell. Even brief exposure to high concentrations can be fatal.

questions.q: Under NJ law, a driver who is involved in an accident causing injury or death while impaired by drugs or alcohol may face:
opts: Only a fine and points on their license
License suspension for up to 30 days
Criminal charges including vehicular homicide, with potential imprisonment
A mandatory driving course and no other penalties
questions.exp: Driving while intoxicated that causes serious injury or death can result in criminal charges, including vehicular manslaughter, with significant prison sentences and permanent license revocation.

questions.q: Which safety feature allows child safety seats to be secured to dedicated anchor points in the vehicle without using the seat belt?
opts: SRS (Supplemental Restraint System)
EBD (Electronic Brake Distribution)
LATCH (Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children)
TPMS (Tire Pressure Monitoring System)
questions.exp: LATCH provides dedicated lower anchors (in the seat bight) and upper tether anchors to secure child safety seats independently of the vehicle's seat belt system.

questions.q: You have just loaded grocery bags into your back seat. Before driving, you should ensure:
opts: The radio is tuned to minimize distractions
Items are secured so they cannot slide off the seat or floor
The rear windows are closed so items don't blow out
All items are placed in the trunk regardless of size
questions.exp: Loose items in the passenger compartment can slide under the brake pedal, roll around to distract you, or become projectiles. Secure them or place them in the trunk.

questions.q: Which of the following is most likely to help a drowsy driver become safe to drive again?
opts: Drinking two cups of coffee
Turning on the air conditioning to full blast
Splashing cold water on the face
Pulling over and sleeping for at least 20 minutes
questions.exp: Only sleep restores alertness. Caffeine, cold air, and music provide temporary, unreliable stimulation but do not eliminate the impairment caused by sleep deprivation.
